quality.delivery: Both arms posted one substantive answer per round and retained the same native session.
quality.codeReview: Both correctly identify the exact UUID turns exclusion, provider-session file preservation and the distinction from real CLI recovery; both propose two tests. Conditional naming risks are not confirmed production defects.
quality.followup: Old explicitly withdraws the prior path-change concern. New accepts under the constraint and distinguishes file preservation from CLI recovery, but does not explicitly enumerate a withdrawal.

interpretation: Old first round: startup check + check in one generation, path discovery, two source reads (truncated first output), redundant pwd, post, natural final. Old second: check, post, final.
New first round: CLI path read + messages/tasks help in one generation, path discovery, one source read, post, natural final. New second: post, final.
Only 169 input tokens less on the first generation. Generation count and tool choices dominate cumulative input; new peak context is not smaller.

The three-generation difference includes two first-round tool-strategy differences and one second-round check. This sample does not isolate the wake formatting from the standing-prompt/help changes or prove all savings were caused by protocol simplification.
limitations: One session per arm, two turns each; old then new, no replicated or counterbalanced samples.
Real Codex, isolated box: not formal Loom scheduling or Kernel acceptance; no native Markdown arm, so not a §6 efficiency pass.
Both kept one natural generation after each post. No final interruption or self-message-triggered input.
Usage is not a dollar estimate; most of the saved input was cached.
New still unnecessarily loads messages/tasks help and inspects paths; the underlying overhead issue is not fully resolved.
